title: Patch: the after-move notice and the hourly sweep never send the same 'your move' twice
thread:
**Issue #4479 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4479: Patch: the after-move notice and the hourly sweep never send the same 'your move' twice
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

A daily game tells you it is your move by email and by phone push. Today two parts of the server can each decide you are due at the same moment: the task that answers a move, and the sweep that runs every hour. When a move lands while a sweep is sending, you get the same "Your move" email twice and the same push on every device twice, and two of the day's shared emails are burned for one event. After this change you get one of each, however the two collide.

## Why

`decide_notify` (the pure decision in `crates/shared`) promises an email at most one per `DAILY_EMAIL_MIN_GAP_HOURS` (6) and a push only when something new waits since the last send, both read off the account's stored `last_email_at` / `last_push_at`. But the promise only holds if one decision runs at a time per account, and two callers run `notify_one` with no exclusion between them:

- the after-move task (`NotifyQueue`, started by `after_move` from `daily/games.rs` and `daily/invites.rs`), and
- the sweep (`sweep()` in `daily/notify.rs`, run by the in-process `run_sweeper` and the Worker's hourly `POST /daily-sweep`, which exclude each other via `DailyState::begin_sweep` but not the queue task).

Both read the same `last_*`, both decide due, both take from the shared `DAILY_PLAYER_EMAILS_PER_DAY` cap (the take is atomic, so the cap holds, but two takes go to one event), both send with fresh random Resend idempotency keys (`daily/{profile}/{new_uuid()}`, so Resend cannot dedupe), and both mark sent. The queue even dedupes within itself (`queued`: two moves before the task reaches a profile decide once), which shows the one-decision-per-wake-up intent; the sweep bypasses that set. The existing tests always drain the queue (`notifier_idle`) before sweeping, so the overlap is untested. The sweep's notify phase walks every holder sequentially with network sends in it, so the window is seconds wide whenever games are active.

## Proposal

Give `notify_one` one per-profile exclusion shared by both callers, held across decide, send and mark-sent (e.g. a per-profile async mutex in `DailyState`, beside `sweeping`). The second caller to arrive for an account waits, then re-reads fresh `last_*` and decides nothing is due, so exactly one email and one push go out. Keep `after_move` enqueue-and-return so a move's answer never waits on mail or push. No migration (in-memory guard is enough: the site runs one server instance), no spec change, no new ruling (an operational race, not a rules decision). Any new number (e.g. a lock wait bound, if one is added) goes in `crates/server/src/config.rs` per rule 9.

## Where it lands

- `crates/server/src/daily/notify.rs` (`notify_one`, `NotifyQueue`, `sweep`)
- `crates/server/src/daily/mod.rs` (`DailyState`, beside `begin_sweep`)
- `crates/server/tests/api/daily.rs` (forced-overlap test; existing cap/gap/release tests stay)
- SPEC §9.13 and §9.8 (the "at most one per `DAILY_EMAIL_MIN_GAP_HOURS`" row); decision logic in `crates/shared/src/notify.rs` is untouched

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A new test forces the overlap (e.g. a paused fake mail/push endpoint, or the guard held open) with an after-move notice and a sweep deciding for the same profile concurrently, and counts exactly one email request and one push per device.
- [ ] The sequential tests keep passing unchanged: queue and sweep share the daily cap, the gap holds, a refused email gives its cap place back.
- [ ] A move's HTTP answer still returns before any mail/push send (enqueue-and-return preserved; the test asserts on ordering or timing).
- [ ] The exclusion is per profile: a stalled send for one account never delays another's (test with two profiles, one stalled).
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-server`, `cargo fmt --check`, and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` are green.

## Size and risks

Size: medium, a day or two: one guard plus tests. Main risk is holding exclusion across network I/O; it is per profile and both paths already send sequentially per profile today, so worst case matches today's latency. Alternative rejected: routing the sweep's notices through `NotifyQueue` and waiting for idle — it would tangle the `/daily-sweep` handler's `Swept` counts and put network sends on the cron's critical path. Alternative rejected: a Postgres advisory lock — heavier and needs lock-semantics tests, for a server that runs as one instance.

## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/45042445322)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Give `notify_one` in `crates/server/src/daily/notify.rs` one per-profile async exclusion, shared by the after-move `NotifyQueue` task and the hourly `sweep`, held across decide, send and mark-sent. The second caller for an account waits, re-reads fresh `last_email_at`/`last_push_at`, and decides nothing is due, so a colliding move and sweep send exactly one email and one push per device. `after_move` stays enqueue-and-return. No spec, ruling, migration, or config change.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/server/src/daily/mod.rs` | change | `DailyState`: new `notify_locks` field, its init in `new()`, and a `notify_lock()` accessor |
| `crates/server/src/daily/notify.rs` | change | `notify_one()` acquires the per-profile guard first; doc comments on `notify_one` and the module header |
| `crates/server/tests/api/daily.rs` | change | Two new tests (overlap exactly-once; per-profile isolation), reusing existing helpers |

Must not touch: `crates/shared/src/notify.rs` (decision logic untouched), `crates/server/src/config.rs` (no new number), anything under `spec/`, `crates/engine`, `crates/cards`, `crates/ai`, `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`. Governing spec: §9.13 (notifications) and §9.8 (push abuse surface) in `spec/09-architecture.md`; no ruling (an operational race, not a rules decision).

## Steps

1. **`crates/server/src/daily/mod.rs` — add the lock map.** Add imports `std::collections::HashMap`, `std::sync::{Arc, Mutex}` (keep the existing `atomic` import). Add field `notify_locks: Mutex<HashMap<String, Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<()>>>>` to `DailyState` with a §9.13 comment (one decision at a time per profile; map holds one entry per profile ever notified, in-memory only, fine for one server instance). Init it as `Mutex::new(HashMap::new())` in `DailyState::new()`.
2. **`crates/server/src/daily/mod.rs` — add the accessor.** Add `pub(crate) fn notify_lock(&self, profile_id: &str) -> Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<()>>`: clone the `Arc` under a brief std-mutex hold using the existing `crate::api::http::lock` helper (as `NotifyQueue::enqueue` does), inserting `Arc::new(tokio::sync::Mutex::new(()))` when absent. Never hold the map mutex across `.await`.
3. **`crates/server/src/daily/notify.rs` — guard `notify_one`.** As the first two lines of `notify_one`, acquire `let guard = app.daily.notify_lock(profile_id);` then `let _held = guard.lock().await;`, so the whole body (reading `waiting`/settings/subs, `decide_notify`, email/push sends, `daily_notify_sent`) runs under the per-profile lock. Update `notify_one`'s doc comment to state the exclusion and that the waiter re-reads fresh state. Both callers (`start()`'s task and `sweep()`'s holder loop) stay sequential and unchanged.
4. **`crates/server/tests/api/daily.rs` — overlap test** `the_after_move_task_and_the_sweep_send_one_profile_one_email_and_push`. Build the app with a `held_service(StatusCode::OK)` mail endpoint (gate closed) plus an immediate `fake_service` push endpoint; one push device each for Ada and Bo (added directly via `tx.push_subs_add`, copying `push_answered`'s endpoint shape). Wrap the `daily_game` accept in `answers_at_once` (proves enqueue-and-return). The queue task takes the acceptor and stalls in the mail send; `eventually` wait for 1 mail request, then `tokio::spawn` `sweep`. Sleep ~1s (lets the sweep reach the guard; mail timeout is 10s, so no timeout risk), then assert exactly 2 mail requests total (queue's acceptor mail plus sweep's challenger mail — the sweep did not double-send for the acceptor). Open the gate (`add_permits(1)`), join the sweep, `notifier_idle`, then assert each `to` address appears exactly once, each push endpoint got exactly one request, both `last_*` are set for both profiles, and `swept == {emailed: 1, pushed: 1}`. Pre-fix this fails (3 mails while gated, 2 per acceptor after).
5. **`crates/server/tests/api/daily.rs` — per-profile test** `a_stalled_send_for_one_account_never_delays_another`. No devices during setup. Game 1 (Bo vs Dan, created first) played past the mulligan until Bo holds; `notifier_idle`. Subscribe Ada's device at a `held_service(StatusCode::CREATED)` push URL and Bo's at an immediate `fake_service` one (Dan/Cy: none). Accept game 2 (Cy challenges, Ada accepts) inside `answers_at_once`; the queue takes Ada and stalls in her push send (`eventually` held==1). Spawn `sweep`; sleep ~1s; assert Bo's endpoint has exactly 1 request while Ada's still has exactly 1 and the sweep is still pending. Open the gate, join, `notifier_idle`; assert Ada's endpoint has exactly 1 total, `swept.pushed == 1`, and Bo's `last_push_at` is set. Creation order (`daily_games_running` orders by `created_at, match_id` in both fake and pg stores) puts Bo first, so a sequential sweep reaches him without touching Ada's lock.
6. **Run the checks** listed in Tests; fix only by changing the new code (never weaken existing tests).

## Tests

- New: `api::daily::the_after_move_task_and_the_sweep_send_one_profile_one_email_and_push` — forces queue/sweep overlap on one profile via a held mail service; asserts 2 mails while gated (one per profile), then exactly one email per recipient and one push per device after the drain.
- New: `api::daily::a_stalled_send_for_one_account_never_delays_another` — Ada's push held, Bo's immediate; asserts Bo's push lands while Ada's send is still held, and Ada is pushed exactly once total.
- Existing (unchanged, must stay green): `api::daily::the_after_move_queue_and_the_sweep_share_the_days_player_email_cap`, `api::daily::an_email_the_mail_service_refused_spends_none_of_the_days_cap`, `api::daily::past_the_days_player_email_cap_the_sweep_still_pushes_and_the_next_day_emails`, `api::daily::a_move_is_answered_before_its_email_goes_and_the_email_still_arrives`, `api::daily::a_profile_queued_twice_before_the_task_reaches_it_is_notified_once`, `api::daily::the_sweep_emails_once_per_account_and_none_when_off_or_without_email`.
- Commands: `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server api::daily::`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

## Done when

- [ ] Overlap test proves one email and one push per device under a forced queue/sweep collision.
- [ ] All sequential cap/gap/release/ordering tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] A move's HTTP answer returns before any send (asserted via `answers_at_once` in the new tests).
- [ ] Per-profile test proves a stalled account never delays another's notice.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server api::daily::`, `cargo fmt --check`, and the clippy command above are green.

## Risks

- Holding the guard across network I/O serializes one account's notices for up to the send timeouts (`PLAYER_EMAIL_TIMEOUT_MS`, `PUSH_TIMEOUT_MS`); accepted per the issue — both paths already send sequentially per profile, so worst case matches today's latency, and failure paths never mark (gap/release semantics unchanged).
- The lock map grows one entry per notified profile and is never pruned; accepted (in-memory only, one instance), noted on the field.
- No deadlock: one leaf-level lock per profile, never nested; `begin_sweep` is an atomic flag, not a mutex, so no lock ordering exists.

## Open questions

None.
```
